description: Library of impossibilities — every killed invention with reusable lessons.
ceo_directive: Eventually the system should possess a library of impossibilities. That could become one of the strongest parts of the entire invention engine.

entries.mechanism_name: Hydraulic state estimation via impedance spectroscopy
entries.what_was_proposed: Estimate 7 hydraulic states (flow, pressure, obstruction, etc.) from impedance measurements at the eShunt surface.
entries.why_it_failed: Structural identifiability proven (Jacobian rank=7), but NUMERICAL non-identifiability under realistic noise (0.5%). Only 1/7 states recoverable. Condition number 1.88e5, parameter correlations >0.95.
entries.reusable_lesson: If the measurement Jacobian is ill-conditioned (>1e4), the system is numerically non-identifiable even if structurally identifiable. Always check condition number AND rank.
entries.what_to_avoid: Do not propose state estimation from collinear measurements without first checking the condition number and noise sensitivity.
entries.physical_constraint: 7 hydraulic states cannot be recovered from impedance measurements under 0.5% noise. The information content of the measurement is insufficient.

entries.what_was_proposed: Combine size-selective membrane with hydrodynamic flow restriction to retain all therapeutic classes.
entries.why_it_failed: Multi-mechanism is Pareto-DOMINATED by hydrodynamic alone for small payloads. Adds engineering complexity without retention benefit for 2 of 3 payload classes.
entries.reusable_lesson: Always compare against the BEST SINGLE mechanism per payload class. A combined mechanism must DOMINATE all singles, not just be 'different'.
entries.what_to_avoid: Do not propose multi-mechanism architectures without proving Pareto-dominance over each single mechanism.

entries.what_was_proposed: Use a 30kDa MWCO membrane to retain large therapeutics (antibody, gene vector, nanoparticle) while CSF drains.
entries.why_it_failed: CSF turnover rate is 2.88x/day. Over 90 days = 259 complete turnovers. Even with 95% retention per pass, therapeutic is washed out: (0.95)^259 ≈ 0. V1's 0.488 retention was a model artifact.
entries.reusable_lesson: Before investing in any retention mechanism, check the CSF TURNOVER RATE. The turnover rate (2.88x/day) is a physiological constant that makes long-term retention physically impossible for any membrane-based mechanism.
entries.what_to_avoid: Do not propose membrane-based or affinity-based retention for >90 day duration. The CSF turnover rate makes it physically impossible.
entries.physical_constraint: CSF turnover rate = 2.88x/day = 259 turnovers in 90 days. No membrane or affinity mechanism can overcome this. The ceiling is PHYSIOLOGICAL (CSF production rate is a constant).

entries.mechanism_name: Derivative and predictive controllers for venous-aware regulation
entries.what_was_proposed: Use ICP derivative (L3d) or predictive model (L5) to regulate drainage based on venous pressure changes.
entries.why_it_failed: L3d: 9.9% M2 reduction vs 15% threshold. L5: 0% M4 reduction. Both mechanisms failed pre-registered buyer boundaries.
entries.reusable_lesson: Derivative-based controllers are too sensitive to noise. Predictive models require accurate forward models that don't exist for CSF dynamics.
entries.what_to_avoid: Do not propose derivative-based or predictive controllers without first proving the signal-to-noise ratio is sufficient.

entries.what_was_proposed: Flow-diverting design to prevent thrombus/fouling accumulation.
entries.why_it_failed: Defeated by El-Shafei retrograde flow on thrombus robustness (5.4x vs NEVER threshold). Retrograde flow can dislodge thrombus → embolization.
entries.reusable_lesson: Any anti-fouling mechanism that relies on flow direction must be tested against RETROGRADE flow. Retrograde flow is a realistic clinical scenario (cough, Valsalva, venous pressure changes).
entries.what_to_avoid: Do not propose flow-direction-dependent anti-fouling without testing retrograde flow robustness.

entries.what_was_proposed: Electrothermal SMA phase-transition activation for shunt retrieval, with thermal isolation and self-test fallback.
entries.why_it_failed: Three independent failure modes: (1) thermal window narrows to 3°C with isolation degradation, (2) sensor electronics SPOF 8% invisible even with dual redundancy, (3) adhesion ceiling 28% failure is biological. V6's 96.97% AVERAGE masked 30% WORST CASE.
entries.reusable_lesson: ALWAYS report worst-case reliability for clinical devices. Averages mask catastrophic failure modes. Thermal activation in a 37°C body environment has a narrow window (37-45°C = 8°C max). Sensor electronics are a SPOF that cannot be fully resolved by redundancy (common-mode failures).
entries.what_to_avoid: Do not propose thermal activation mechanisms for implantable devices without (a) proving the thermal window is >8°C, (b) resolving sensor SPOF to <5% invisible, (c) addressing adhesion ceiling with non-snare mechanism.

entries.what_was_proposed: Flexible (compliant) segment between rigid eShunt body and venous anchoring point to reduce mechanical trauma.
entries.why_it_failed: Problem existence failure (Article XX). Rigid eShunt body is 1890x stiffer than venous wall — vein deforms around shunt, shunt does NOT impose bending stress. M5 solves a HYPOTHETICAL problem. Also introduces kink risk (-5° safety margin) and fatigue embolization.
entries.reusable_lesson: Before optimizing a solution, VERIFY THE PROBLEM EXISTS at the physics level. The IVC filter analogy (cantilevered) does not apply to the eShunt (both-ends-anchored supported beam). A compliant tube deforms around a rigid object, not the other way around.
entries.what_to_avoid: Do not propose compliant/flexible interfaces for both-ends-anchored implants in compliant vessels. The problem (bending trauma) doesn't exist in this geometry. Do not use analogies from cantilevered devices (IVC filters) for supported-beam devices (eShunt).
entries.physical_constraint: Rigid eShunt (EI=1.6e-1) is 1890x stiffer than venous wall (EI=8.4e-5). The vein conforms to the shunt. No bending stress is transmitted.

entries.mechanism_name: M5_REFINED adaptive over-drainage controller (sleep-state + venous pressure)
entries.what_was_proposed: Adaptive drainage controller using ICP + venous pressure sensors to prevent over-drainage during sleep.
entries.why_it_failed: Problem existence undetermined. The eShunt drains subarachnoid→venous sinus (short path, no hydrostatic column, 7 mmHg differential). Over-drainage is siphon-driven in VP shunts; the eShunt may not have a siphon effect. The valve closes at 7 mmHg (above 5 mmHg over-drainage threshold). BUT: device is too new (first-in-human 2021), insufficient clinical data.
entries.reusable_lesson: Do not assume VP shunt problems apply to the eShunt. The eShunt's drainage geometry is fundamentally different (short path, no siphon). Always verify the problem exists for the SPECIFIC device geometry. Over-drainage is siphon-driven; without a hydrostatic column, it may not occur.
entries.what_to_avoid: Do not propose over-drainage prevention mechanisms for the eShunt without first establishing that over-drainage occurs in the eShunt specifically (not just in VP shunts). The eShunt's short drainage path may inherently prevent the siphon effect.
entries.physical_constraint: eShunt normal CSF-venous differential = 7 mmHg. Valve closes at P_venous + P_valve = 2 + 5 = 7 mmHg (upright), above 5 mmHg over-drainage threshold. Without a hydrostatic column, over-drainage may be physically prevented.

entries.what_was_proposed: Endovascular catheter with mechanical snare/grasper engages the eShunt and applies traction for removal. No thermal activation, no electronic sensors, no adhesion dependence.
entries.why_it_failed: Tissue ingrowth is the SAME adhesion ceiling as M3. IVC filter retrieval success drops to ~50% at 6 months. Embolization from tissue fragments conflicts with CE-007 zero-embolization. Not novel (FlowTriever/snares established). Poor failure recovery (craniotomy).
entries.reusable_lesson: Changing retrieval ACTIVATION does NOT change retrieval PHYSICS. Any retrieval mechanism for a permanently implanted endovascular anchor faces the same ingrowth ceiling. The problem is not HOW you pull — it is that the anchor is DESIGNED to be ingrown.
entries.what_to_avoid: Do not propose retrieval mechanisms for permanently implanted endovascular anchors without addressing tissue ingrowth. The ingrowth is by design.
entries.physical_constraint: eShunt anchor designed for tissue ingrowth. Retrieval after 6+ months has ~50% success (IVC filter data). Tissue fragments during retrieval conflict with zero-embolization threshold.

entries.what_was_proposed: Retrograde flush from venous side to clear obstruction. eShunt stays in place, no device removal needed.
entries.why_it_failed: Retrograde flush pushes obstruction debris INTO the subarachnoid space (brain). V11.1 quantitative model: 100% particle SAS entry, 970/1000 >10um. V11.2 CORRECTION: USP <788> 9.7x comparison RETRACTED (USP applies to parenteral, not intrathecal). Replaced with analogical evidence: 152 SAH inflammation studies, 33 arachnoiditis studies. CLEARS device (2025) confirms retrograde flush is already known for VP shunts. eShunt venous drainage makes retrograde inherently more dangerous (debris to brain vs peritoneum).
entries.reusable_lesson: Retrograde flush for eShunt pushes debris toward brain. The eShunt venous drainage direction makes retrograde more dangerous than VP shunts (peritoneal). However, the clinical hazard is ANALOGICAL (SAH blood causes inflammation), not directly proven for shunt debris. MODEL_DERIVED + ANALOGICAL_EVIDENCE — not PROVEN_UNSAFE.
entries.what_to_avoid: Do not propose retrograde flush or debris-mobilizing clearing for eShunt without addressing the brain-ward debris transport. Safe clearing mechanisms must push debris DISTALLY (toward venous system).
entries.physical_constraint: eShunt drains subarachnoid→venous. Retrograde = venous→subarachnoid = debris to brain. 100% of modeled particles enter SAS. Clinical hazard supported by analogy (SAH, arachnoiditis), not direct shunt-debris evidence.

entries.what_was_proposed: eShunt anchor contains magnetic element. External magnetic field (MRI or electromagnet) applies force to disengage anchor.
entries.why_it_failed: MRI compatibility is a GATEKEEPER for neurosurgical implants (hydrocephalus patients need brain MRI). Magnetic element causes premature release, heating, torque, image artifact. Magnetic force at 5-10cm depth (1/r3 decay) is 10-50x less than needed for ingrowth disengagement (0.05-0.1N available vs 1-5N required). Demagnetization ~1%/year. Partial release creates new failure mode.
entries.reusable_lesson: Magnetic actuation is incompatible with neurosurgical implants that must coexist with brain MRI. The 1/r3 force decay makes deep-tissue magnetic actuation fundamentally insufficient. Any mechanism requiring external magnetic actuation for a deep endovascular implant faces both MRI safety and force-distance constraints.
entries.what_to_avoid: Do not propose magnetic actuation for neurosurgical implants requiring MRI compatibility. Do not propose magnetic mechanisms for deep-tissue (>3cm) actuation where 1/r3 force decay makes mechanism insufficient.
entries.physical_constraint: MRI field (1.5-3T) exerts force on magnetic element causing premature release. Force at 5-10cm depth: 0.05-0.1N (available) vs 1-5N (required). 1/r3 distance dependence is a physics constant.

entries.mechanism_name: R2-C3 predictor v1 — pressure-trajectory + phenotype classification for VSS failure-type prediction
entries.what_was_proposed: Use pre-treatment or early post-treatment physiological measurements (CSF opening pressure, venous pressure gradient, pressure trajectory over time) combined with headache phenotype classification to predict which specific failure phenotype (R2-C1/C2/C3/C4/C5) a VSS-stented IIH patient will develop, early enough to change the salvage treatment decision.
entries.why_it_failed: Three independent failures: (1) §103 SERIOUS THREAT — the Hakim self-adjusting-valve family (WO2020086847A1, US20210379344A1) already claims CSF pressure + venous pressure + differential calculation + continuous monitoring (trajectory) + closed-loop valve control + IIH treatment. The proposed 'pressure trajectory → failure-type classifier' uses the SAME measurements for a different analytical purpose. Without a new technical effect, this is 'AI applied to an existing clinical variable.' (2) NO NEW TECHNICAL PRIMITIVE — no genuinely new signal source found. CGRP as a pre-treatment biomarker was tested and found not presently established (conflicting evidence: one negative study, one positive case series). Other candidates (ICHD-3 headache phenotype, multi-site venous distribution, intra-procedural response) are untested with no available data. (3) DECISION-VALUE TEST FAILS — Q2 (earlier-than-routine prediction) = NO (requires post-VSS LP which clinicians already perform); Q3 (improves decision) = UNKNOWN/NEGATIVE (proposed CGRP mAb salvage treatment has conflicting evidence).
entries.reusable_lesson: FROZEN THEOREM (sharpened per CEO Round 56o): 'Existing information + existing transformation + existing control, merely recombined, is insufficient. A combination qualifies only if it produces a demonstrably new technical effect that survives prior art and non-obviousness attack. A world-class invention needs a genuinely new technical information source, transformation, or control capability. Do not build an AI layer on top of an already-claimed sensing/control architecture.' NOTE: This theorem does NOT create a universal 'new sensor required' rule. A novel combination of existing measurements CAN qualify if it produces a new, technically non-obvious effect. The theorem rejects TRIVIAL recombination, not all combinations.
what_to_avoid: Do not propose AI classification of physiological variables that are already measured and controlled by existing patent claims (Hakim family).
Do not assume that 'measuring the same thing for a different purpose' constitutes a new technical effect.
Do not propose CGRP as a pre-treatment discriminator without acknowledging the conflicting evidence (2022 negative study vs 2025 positive case series).
Do not propose a salvage treatment pathway without establishing that the salvage treatment itself works (CGRP mAb evidence is conflicting).
evidence_sources: US20040267187A1 / US7318813B2 (Rosenberg/Codman — self-adjusting valve with pressure-over-time)
Lakhani 2026 (PMID 41879313 — symptom phenotype → VSS readmission risk)
Physicians Weekly 2025 (CGRP levels not significant between IIH and controls)
Neurology Live 2022 (CGRP mAbs no significant impact on persistent IIH headache)
entries.cgp_correction: CGRP as the proposed discriminator is NOT PERMANENTLY KILLED. The correct classification is 'not presently established.' A single negative/limited study kills that specific evidentiary basis, not the entire biomarker category. Future evidence may re-open CGRP as a discriminator if: (a) a larger study finds significance, (b) CGRP is combined with other biomarkers, or (c) CGRP is measured in a different compartment (CSF vs serum).

entries.territory_id: CV-T05 (R2-C3 phenotype discovery, Round 56 orthogonal search)
entries.mechanism_name: OSV-4: HRV/autonomic state as orthogonal predictor for R2-C3
entries.what_was_proposed: Use heart rate variability (HRV) as a genuinely orthogonal physiological signal (from the autonomic/cardiac system) to predict R2-C3 phenotype after VSS, on the theory that autonomic dysfunction might identify patients whose headache persists despite ICP normalization.
entries.why_it_failed: Three independent failures: (1) CAUSAL PATHWAY REVERSIBLE — Schmidt 2018 (PMID 29472865, cited 149x) establishes that ICP is a 'REVERSIBLE determinant of efferent sympathetic outflow.' If post-VSS ICP normalizes, sympathetic activity should reverse too. In R2-C3 (ICP already normal), sympathetic activity should already be normal. HRV cannot distinguish R2-C3 (normal ICP + headache) from controls (normal ICP + no headache). (2) PROXY FOR ICP — Schmidt 2018 shows HRV is driven by ICP ('ICP is a determinant of sympathetic activity'). If ICP is already measured (Hakim), HRV is a NOISIER VERSION of ICP, not an independent signal. This is the same pattern as CE-012: 'existing measurement + new purpose.' (3) NO NEW DECISION — if HRV is a proxy for ICP, no new decision is enabled that ICP doesn't already enable.
entries.reusable_lesson: A signal can be GENUINELY ORTHOGONAL to a specific measurement architecture (Hakim measures pressure, not HRV) and still be a DOWNSTREAM CONSEQUENCE of the same physiological variable (ICP → sympathetic → HRV). Orthogonality to one architecture does not imply independence from the underlying physiology. Before claiming a signal is 'new information,' test whether it is causally downstream of an already-measured variable. If A → B and A is measured, then B is a proxy for A, not new information — even if B is measured by a different sensor.
what_to_avoid: Do not assume a signal from a different physiological system is independent just because it uses a different sensor.
Do not propose HRV or autonomic markers as predictors of conditions driven by ICP without first establishing that the autonomic change PERSISTS after ICP normalization.
Do not assume 'orthogonal to one patent' means 'independent of the measured variable.'
entries.physical_constraint: ICP is a reversible determinant of sympathetic activity (Schmidt 2018). HRV reflects ICP-driven sympathetic changes. In the R2-C3 phenotype (ICP normal), HRV should be normal because the driving variable (ICP) is normal.
evidence_sources: Schmidt 2018 (PMID 29472865, Front Physiol) — 'ICP Is a Determinant of Sympathetic Activity'

entries.mechanism_name: RES-4 broad: adaptive cerebrospinal venous stent with sensing + flow regulation
entries.what_was_proposed: Adaptive venous sinus stent with sensor + microprocessor + variable diameter + closed-loop control for dynamic venous outflow regulation in IIH. The broad claim was that 'dynamic venous outflow regulation' is a new technical effect not achievable by shunts or static stents.
entries.why_it_failed: US11304793B2 (priority 2010-02-10, active until 2031) materially occupies the broad architecture. Claim 1 covers: self-expanding stent in cerebrospinal vein + sensor detecting physiological trigger (rising venous backpressure) + microprocessor automatically actuating stent to variable force + deformable constraining member for post-implant tunability + closed-loop (sensor→processor→actuation). The 12-search prior-art attack in Round 56q MISSED this patent because the search used internally coined terminology ('adaptive venous stent', 'sensing stent') rather than the patent's actual language ('cerebrospinal venous insufficiency', 'tunable endovascular device', 'deformable constraining member').
entries.reusable_lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-014: 'No result for our formulation is not evidence that the capability is absent. Patent searches must generate terminology from patent claims + descriptions + CPC classes + inventor vocabulary + adjacent technologies, not just internally coined phrases. A query-fragile search produces false negatives.' The machine must be better at discovering what competitors actually claimed than it is at inventing elegant names for what we hope is new.
what_to_avoid: Do not conclude 'no prior art found' based on keyword searches using internally coined terminology.
Do not assume that the absence of results for our formulation means the capability is novel.

Future patent searches must include: (a) CPC class traversal, (b) inventor/assignee neighbor search, (c) adjacent technology terminology, (d) backward/forward citation chains, not just keyword matching.
Do not propose 'adaptive stent' or 'sensing stent' architectures without first searching CCSVI/MS patent literature, which uses different vocabulary for the same concepts.
evidence_sources: US11304793B2 (priority 2010-02-10, active 2031) — adaptive cerebrospinal vein stent with sensor + microprocessor + variable expansion
entries.narrow_gap_surviving: The narrow gap (adaptive transverse/sigmoid sinus stent for IIH, specifically regulating CSF absorption at the arachnoid granulation site) is NOT killed. US11304793B2 covers IJV (extracranial) for MS, not transverse/sigmoid sinus (intracranial) for IIH. The physiological effect may be different (CSF absorption regulation vs venous return regulation). But §103 risk is SERIOUS (obvious anatomical transfer).
